mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate (as of t-1mo) is inversely related to S&P 500 forward returns: higher rates compress equity valuations through increased discount rates, leading to negative returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is at its current level (4.1%) or higher, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL value above 300 (as of t-1mo) indicates persistent inflation, prompting a hawkish monetary policy response that increases equity risk premiums, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 300, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The joint behavior of rising FEDFUNDS and high CPIAUCSL (both as of t-1mo) signals a tightening monetary cycle that increases risk aversion and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL are above their respective thresholds (FEDFUNDS > 4.0 and CPIAUCSL > 295), or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of tight labor market (UNRATE < 3.6%) and strong industrial production (INDPRO > 104.0 as of t-2mo), the S&P 500 is expected to produce positive returns over the next 60 trading days due to robust corporate earnings growth and low recession risk.
regime_hint: late-cycle expansion with tight labor market
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE < 3.6 and INDPRO > 104.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The unemployment rate (as of t-1mo) is inversely related to S&P 500 forward returns: lower unemployment rates indicate a strong labor market that supports corporate earnings, leading to positive returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE is at its current level (3.5%) or lower, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A HOUST value below 1400 (as of t-2mo) signals a weakening housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic slowdown, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when HOUST < 1400, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between rising industrial production (INDPRO) and falling residential sales (RSAFS) signals a supply-demand mismatch that increases market volatility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO is rising and RSAFS is falling, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 295) with the Federal Reserve cutting rates (FEDFUNDS < 4.0), the S&P 500 is expected to produce positive returns over the next 60 trading days as the market prices in a soft landing scenario.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 295 and FEDFUNDS < 4.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
